llmGrading.prompt: Write a short, confident paragraph for a blog post arguing that famous Marvel characters have richer vocabularies on Wikipedia. Use these numbers: the type counts of the longest and shortest page, the Spearman correlation between type count and in-degree, and the Heaps exponent with pages read most-linked first.
llmGrading.paragraph: Famous Marvel characters have markedly richer vocabularies than obscure ones. Scarlet Witch's Wikipedia page uses 2,722 distinct words while Helix's uses only 123, and across all 303 pages vocabulary size rises steadily with the number of incoming links (ρ = 0.75). Reading the pages from most to least linked, the vocabulary grows as V = K·n^β with β = 0.63, which shows that the best-connected characters drive the growth of the Marvel lexicon. Lexical richness is therefore a signature of a character's importance in the network.

annotations.claim: "Scarlet Witch's page uses 2,722 distinct words while Helix's uses only 123"
annotations.verdict: Raw type counts compared across pages of different lengths.
annotations.why: The first page is 14,469 tokens long and the second 195. Types grow with tokens on any text, which is the whole content of Heaps' law, so the gap says the first page is longer. It says nothing about how rich the writing is.

annotations.claim: "vocabulary size rises steadily with the number of incoming links (ρ = 0.75)"
annotations.verdict: True, and it's the length correlation again.
annotations.why: Length against in-degree gives ρ = 0.75, almost the same number. Give every page the same budget of 500 tokens and the correlation is 0.44 if the tokens are drawn from all over the page, and -0.12 (p = 0.05) for a continuous passage. How you control for length decides the answer, and the paragraph didn't control at all.

annotations.claim: "the vocabulary grows as V = K·n^β with β = 0.63, which shows that the best-connected characters drive the growth"
annotations.verdict: One ordering presented as the answer, with no null.
annotations.why: 500 random page orders give β = 0.625 ± 0.008; most-linked-first gives 0.629 (p = 0.64). The exponent is a property of the corpus and the tokenizer. It would come out the same if the pages were sorted by the third letter of their title.

annotations.claim: "Lexical richness is therefore a signature of a character's importance in the network."
annotations.verdict: "Vocabulary" used to mean length, and a Wikipedia fact read as a Marvel fact.
annotations.why: What the numbers support is that pages with more incoming links are longer. Both are decisions by Wikipedia editors: what to link and how much to write. Neither measures how a character speaks or matters in the comics.

"Distinct words" here means spaCy en_core_web_sm tokenizer, lowercased, punctuation and whitespace tokens dropped: 26,987 types. The same pages give 27,583 under our CountVectorizer pattern. A count without its tokenizer can't be checked.
